'''''Aizoanthemopsis hispanica''''', or '''Spanish aizoon''', is a [[species]] of flowering plant in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Aizoaceae]]. It is the sole species in genus '''''Aizoanthemopsis'''''.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Aizoanthemopsis'' Klak {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77173703-1 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |access-date=13 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> It is a succulent native to northern Africa, the Mediterranean region and the Middle East where it grows on arid sandy plains, saline areas and in semi-arid habitats.

It was [[Species description|first described]] as ''Aizoon hispanicum'' by the Swedish naturalist [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. In 2002 it was placed in the genus ''[[Aizoanthemum]]'' by the German botanist [[Heidrun Hartmann]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=20004141-1&back_page=%2Fipni%2FeditSimplePlantNameSearch.do%3Ffind_wholeName%3DAizoanthemum%2Bhispanicum%26output_format%3Dnormal |title=''Aizoanthemum hispanicum'' |publisher=International Plant Names Index |access-date=1 March 2016}}</ref> In 2017 Cornelia Klak placed the species in the newly-described [[monotypic taxon|monotypic genus]] ''Aizoanthemopsis''.<ref name = powo/>

==Description==
''A. hispanica'' is a sprawling annual herbaceous plant {{convert|5|to|20|cm|in|0|abbr=on}} high with opposite, papillose, succulent leaves. These are lanceolate with entire margins. The solitary flowers have five white [[tepal]]s which are yellowish green on the outside, 5 to 15 [[stamen]]s and an ovary with 5 [[locule]]s giving a pentagonal fruit capsule containing 2 brown seeds in each locule.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sahara-nature.com/plantes.php?aff=nom&plante=aizoon%20hispanicum |title=''Aizoon hispanicum'' |work=Sahara-Nature |access-date=1 March 2016}}</ref><ref name=Israel>{{cite web |url=http://www.flowersinisrael.com/Aizoonhispanicum_page.htm |title=''Aizoon hispanicum'', ''Aizoanthemum hispanicum'', Aizoon, Spanish aizoon |author=Modzelevich, Martha |work=Flowers in Israel |access-date=1 March 2016}}</ref>

The fruits have an unusual mechanism for dispersing the seeds. When it rains, the locules gradually fill with water. Near the centre of the capsule, the covering membranes are arranged in such a way that they form a nozzle, and when further rain drops fall on the capsule, a jet of water and seeds is propelled through this nozzle; this allows the plant to scatter its seeds much more widely than is the case in related species that lack this mechanism.<ref name=Israel/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''A. hispanica'' is native to [[Egypt]], [[Israel]], [[Jordan]], [[Syria]], [[Cyprus]], [[Turkey]], [[Iraq]], [[Iran]] and the Arabian Peninsula where it grows in compacted sandy soil in desert plains, saline areas and semi-arid regions.<ref>{{cite book|author=Daoud |title=Flora of Kuwait |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=X85dAgAAQBAJ&pg=RA1-PA20 |year=2013 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-84881-3 |page=20}}</ref> It also grows in the Mediterranean region and the Canary Islands.<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |url=http://eol.org/pages/5166877/details |title=''Aizoon hispanicum'' |encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of Life |access-date=2 March 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.floradecanarias.com/aizoon_hispanicum.html |title=''Aizoon hispanicum'' L.  |work=Flora vascular de Canarias |access-date=2 March 2016}}</ref>

==Ecology==
It has been found that the seeds of ''A. hispanica'' germinate poorly in the laboratory when placed on a filter paper in the dark at {{convert|30|°C}}. The germination rate can be improved by placing some soil nearby, by covering the seeds for a few days and then uncovering them, or by placing some covered seeds nearby. This suggests that both soil and covered seeds give out some gas, possibly [[ethylene]], which stimulates germination in nearby uncovered seeds.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Gat-Tilman, G. |year=1994 |title=Soil gases and the germination of ''Aizoon hispanicum'' |journal=Journal of Arid Environments |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=39–44 |doi=10.1016/S0140-1963(05)80019-9 |bibcode=1994JArEn..28...39G }}</ref>
